11   witness, I could and would competently testify thereto.
12         2.      I submit this declaration in response to the Court’s Order to Show
13   Cause (“OSC”).

15   did not timely comply with Court pre-trial deadlines, and why this case should not
16   be dismissed for failure to prosecute.

18   follows:

25                 a Notice of Appearance.
26              d. Rabiya Tirmizi – became an attorney of record on 5/5/25 with a
27                 Notice of Appearance (ECF 23). On 3/31/26 a Notice of Change in

 7         5.      This matter was removed by Defendant FCA US LLC (“Defendant”)
 8   from the Santa Clara Superior Court on September 5, 2024 (ECF 1). Shortly after
 9   removal I became aware of this case.
10         6.      The case was originally assigned to the Honorable P. Casey Pitts. It
11   was reassigned to Your Honor on February 4, 2025 (ECF 19).
12         7.      I coordinated with Defendant’s counsel to prepare the Joint Case
13   Management Statement, which was timely filed on November 17, 2024, and then
14   again on March 17, 2025, after reassignment of the case. Ms. Tirmizi attended the
15   Initial Case Management Conference. The Scheduling Order was issued on May
16   6, 2025 (ECF 25). The Final Pretrial Conference was set for April 1, 2026.
17         8.      Prior to the pretrial deadlines, I was actively working with opposing
18   counsel to complete discovery. The Parties exchanged written discovery. The
19   Parties worked together to schedule deposition on mutually agreeable dates. Due
20   to the high volume of cases and relative scarcity of Rule 30(b) (6) witnesses and
21   experts to attend the vehicle inspection, there was ongoing communication
22   between the Parties to try to arrange the same and reschedule after cancellations.
23   Thus, the Parties have been actively pursuing this matter and were actively
24   engaged in discovery.
25         9.      The deadline to complete ADR was set for August 15, 2026 (ECF
26   25). The Parties engaged in mediation with Grant Woodruff on August 13, 2025.
27   The mediation did not result in a settlement offer. Defendant did provide a Rule
28   68 offer on or around March 24, 2026, which did not result in settlement.

 1         10.      Prior to the pretrial deadlines, I was actively working with opposing
 2   counsel to complete discovery. Due to the high volume of cases and relative
 3   scarcity of Rule 30(b) (6) witnesses and experts to attend the vehicle inspection,
 4   there was frequent communication between the Parties to try to arrange the same
 5   and reschedule after cancellations. Thus, the Parties have been actively pursuing
 6   this matter and were actively engaged in the discovery process.
 7         11.      Due to the April 1, 2026, date of the Final Pretrial Conference, I
 8   believed the trial team was actively handling this matter in preparation for trial.
 9   However, on March 19, 2026, I received an email from opposing counsel
10   indicating that we had missed the deadline to file the Pretrial Statement. I
11   immediately forwarded that email to Mr. Chae to bring the issue to his attention so
12   that he could address it as I knew Mr. Chae was lead trial attorney in this matter.
13   It is my understanding that Mr. Chae did in fact immediately reach out to
14   opposing counsel to prepare the pretrial documents.
15         12.      I am assigned to handle a matter from the time it is removed to
16   federal court through the end of fact discovery. Thereafter, the matter gets
17   assigned to the trial team for expert discovery, preparation of trial documents and
18   to attend the pretrial conference and trial. It was my understanding and belief that
19   the trial team was preparing the pretrial documents as required.
20         13.      I have been subject to the following sanctions:

26               was sanctioned on February 28, 2025, in the Southern District of
27               California in the amount of $500.00. The sanction was timely paid on
28               March 10, 2025.

16 counsel, do not supervise SLP’s trial team, and do not oversee trial-related filings.

17 SLP has a separate trial team that is responsible for handling trial-related filings and

18 trials. It is my understanding that those attorneys will appear in any federal matters

19 sufficiently in advance of any trial related work necessary to the case and meet all

20 deadlines.

21        4.     As part of my supervision of this case in its pre-trial phase, I reviewed
22 and signed the Complaint, drafted by former SLP associate Sanam Vaziri, making the

23 two of us attorneys of record when the case was removed to this Court on September

27 reviewing firm records.

12 discussions with my colleagues, the pre-trial deadlines were docketed and delegated

15 of this case for trial, meeting and conferring, and would ensure that the trial

16 documents would be timely submitted in compliance with this Court’s orders. Mr.

17 Chae is filing a supplemental declaration to explain how the lapse occurred that

18 resulted in his late appearance and pre-trial filings.

19        9.     However, I regret that I did not discover the issue sooner and apologize

21 of judicial resources. I apologize to the Court for this and have escalated the issue

22 internally so that the firm can improve internal processes.

25 Chae for trial purposes and to help ensure the matter proceeds smoothly on a going

26 forward basis. As a result, his appearance was filed on March 23, 2026 (Dkt. 29).

19         I, Mark W. Skanes, declare:
20         1.     I am an attorney duly licensed to practice law before all of the courts of the
21   State of California and the United States District Court for the Northern District of
22   California, and I am a partner with ROSEWALDORF LLP, attorney of record for
23   Defendant FCA US LLC (“FCA US”) in this action. I am a member in good standing
24   with the State Bar of California.
25         2.     I have personal knowledge of the following facts, except for those based
26   upon information and belief, which I believe to be true, and if called upon to testify, I
27   would and could competently testify to their truth and accuracy.
28         3.     This Declaration is submitted in response to this Court’s Order to Show
                                               1
       DECLARATION OF MARK W. SKANES IN RESPONSE TO ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE, DATED APRIL 1, 2026
             Case 5:24-cv-06274-NW       Document 46     Filed 04/10/26   Page 2 of 7




 1   Cause, dated April 1, 2026 (Doc. 41).
 2         4.       RoseWaldorf LLP was retained by FCA US to defend its interests in this
 3   matter.     I was initially assigned to this matter, along with an associate, Claudia
 4   Gavrilescu, Esq.
 5         5.       On September 5, 2024, I worked with Attorney Gavrilescu on completing
 6   and filing the Notice of Removal of this matter to this Court.
 7         6.       Upon removal, the case was initially assigned to the Honorable Virginia K.
 8   DeMarchi (Doc. 5).
 9         7.       Thereafter, the case was reassigned to the Honorable P. Casey Pitts (Doc.
10   8).
11         8.       On February 24, 2025, the case was reassigned a third time to the Honorable
12   Noel Wise.
13         9.       Upon reassignment to Judge Wise, our office calendared the relevant
14   deadlines in Judge Wise’s Pretrial Order (Doc. 25).
15         10.      Similar to this Court’s reassignment of this matter, RoseWaldorf LLP
16   reassigned the matter internally as well.
17         11.      Specifically, given the dramatic increase in volume of Song-Beverly based
18   matters filed in the past year, RoseWaldorf LLP hired several more attorneys, paralegals
19   and litigation secretaries to help reduce case counts and more actively manage litigation
20   matters.
21         12.      In January of 2026, RoseWaldorf started the process of transferring this
22   matter, among many others, to other lead handling attorneys within the firm.
23         13.      On February 24, 2026, this matter (along with several others) was
24   reassigned from me to another partner in the firm, Michael Mehall, Esq., for
25   management. For consistency, Attorney Gavrilescu remained assigned to the matter,
26   along with several of the assigned supporting staff members.
27         14.      A team of paralegals and support staff were tasked with preparing notices
28   of appearances for Attorney Mehall and withdrawals for the undersigned counsel in the

                                               2
       DECLARATION OF MARK W. SKANES IN RESPONSE TO ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE, DATED APRIL 1, 2026
             Case 5:24-cv-06274-NW      Document 46      Filed 04/10/26    Page 3 of 7




 1   various matters that were reassigned.
 2         15.    Due to a backlog of matters, however, the appearance/withdrawal formally
 3   reflecting the change of partner overseeing this matter was not filed with this Court prior
 4   to the March 18, 2026 deadline for the filing of the Joint Pretrial Statement.
 5         16.    Nevertheless, on March 10, 2026, this matter was part of an internal audit
 6   of cases and Attorney Gavrilescu and the team of paralegals working on this matter
 7   confirmed the deadlines set forth in the Pretrial Order (Doc. 25).
 8         17.    In addition, the March 18, 2026 deadline to confirm the filing of the Joint
 9   Pretrial Statement was calendared in the firm’s master calendar and was assigned to
10   Attorney Gavrilescu.
11         18.    Although as of March 18, 2026, the docket did not reflect the change in
12   handling attorney, the change to Attorney Mehall as the partner assigned was reflected
13   internally on RoseWaldorf’s file management system.
14         19.    Therefore, I reasonably relied upon this internal reassignment, and it was
15   my belief that necessary deadlines, including the March 18, 2026 Joint Pretrial Statement
16   Deadline, would be met.
17         20.    In the numerous other matters our office has with Strategic Legal Practices
18   (“SLP”), our pattern and practice regarding trial documents has been that SLP prepares
19   the initial draft of joint pre-trial documents and our office provides comments, changes
20   and additions as necessary.
21         21.    Upon information and belief, our office relied upon this pattern and practice
22   with SLP and was awaiting SLP’s version of the trial documents in this matter for our
23   input, additions and changes.
24         22.    In this matter, however, our office never received the initial draft of the
25   Joint Pretrial Statement from SLP prior to the March 18, 2026 deadline.
26         23.    Upon information and belief, our office did not receive any efforts by SLP
27   to meet and confer prior to the March 18, 2026 deadline.
28         24.    Upon information and belief, Attorney Gavrilescu did not prepare and file

                                               3
       DECLARATION OF MARK W. SKANES IN RESPONSE TO ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE, DATED APRIL 1, 2026
             Case 5:24-cv-06274-NW       Document 46     Filed 04/10/26    Page 4 of 7




 1   the Joint Pretrial Statement on or before March 18, 2026, as she believed it was
 2   Plaintiff’s counsel’s obligation to prepare and circulate the joint statement.
 3         25.    Furthermore, despite the transfer of matters internally, I would frequently
 4   follow up with the team of reassigned attorneys and paralegals to confirm that deadlines
 5   were being met. However, on March 18, 2026, I was out of the office for a majority of
 6   the day due to complications from a recent minor surgery. Therefore, I did not conduct
 7   a second review of all calendar deadlines for that day or inquire as to whether as I might
 8   have normally done to ensure that the Joint Pretrial Statement was filed.
 9         26.    Upon information and belief, on March 19, 2026, Attorney Mehall realized
10   the deadline to file the Joint Pretrial Statement in this matter had passed and immediately
11   asked Attorney Gavrilescu to meet and confer with SLP regarding the Joint Pretrial
12   Statement and the remaining trial documents.
13         27.    On March 23, 2026, I reviewed the Court’s Order to Show Cause (Doc. 28)
14   and believed the matter was directed towards Plaintiff, as the threatened sanction was
15   dismissal “for failure to prosecute” (id.). The Order required “the parties” to appear in
16   person for the hearing on April 1, 2026 – the date of the Final Pretrial Conference.
17         28.    At that time, Attorney Mehall assigned Attorney Glen Olives as lead trial
18   counsel in this matter. Given that lead trial counsel is typically required to appear at the
19   final pretrial conference (that was previously scheduled for the same day, April 1, 2026),
20   Attorney Olives appeared for the April 1, 2026 hearing.
21         29.    Additionally, for the sake of consistency, Attorney Olives submitted a
22   Declaration in response to the Court’s March 23, 2026 Order to Show cause.
23         30.    Had I known that the Court required my appearance at the April 1, 2026
24   hearing, I would have appeared.
25         31.    In further response to the Court’s April 1, 2026 Order, I hereby provide
26   notice that I was personally sanctioned in the following matters:
27                   a. Caldwell v. FCA US LLC, Case No.: CU24-09230 (Solano County
28                       Superior Court). By Order, dated January 16, 2026, I was sanctioned

                                               4
       DECLARATION OF MARK W. SKANES IN RESPONSE TO ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE, DATED APRIL 1, 2026
             Case 5:24-cv-06274-NW      Document 46      Filed 04/10/26   Page 5 of 7




 1                       $350 for failure to timely file a Settlement Conference Statement.
 2                       The sanctions payment was due on or before February 13, 2026, and
 3                       the sanction was paid on January 23, 2026.
 4                    b. Gonzalez v. FCA US LLC, Case No.: 22LBCV00491 (Los Angeles
 5                       County Superior Court). By Order, dated October 25, 2023, I was
 6                       sanctioned $250 for failure to consummate a settlement. Sanctions
 7                       were due on or before November 27, 2023, and the sanction was paid
 8                       on November 2, 2023.
 9                    c. Bell v. FCA US LLC, Case No.: CV0003980 (Marin County Superior
10                       Court). By Order, dated February 28, 2025, I was sanctioned $149
11                       for failing to appear for a Case Management Conference. Sanctions
12                       were due by March 11, 2025, and the sanction was paid on March
13                       10, 2025.
14         32.    I am unaware of any non-monetary sanction being imposed upon me
15   personally and I am unaware of any instance where a court found that I personally
16   breached any rules of professional conduct.
17         33.    I reiterate that due to the unprecedented increase in the number of Song-
18   Beverly matters being filed in California state and federal courts in recent years,
19   RoseWaldorf has continually hired additional attorneys, paralegals and staff to
20   accommodate the influx of new matters. In addition, RoseWaldorf has transferred
21   matters internally, like this matter, to other attorneys for handling to ensure proper
22   management of cases. This includes the transfer of files from one partner to another, like
23   here, in order to coordinate more significant file management efforts.
24         34.    I, along with the entire firm, will continue those efforts to ensure that no
25   further deadlines in this matter or others are missed.
26         35.    I sincerely apologize to the Court and respectfully requests that no sanctions
27   are issued in this matter.
28         36.    Furthermore, I am a resident of the State of New York and the personal

                                               5
       DECLARATION OF MARK W. SKANES IN RESPONSE TO ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE, DATED APRIL 1, 2026
             Case 5:24-cv-06274-NW         Document 46   Filed 04/10/26   Page 6 of 7




 1   appearance before this Court on April 20, 2026 already presents a significant financial
 2   burden and personal hardship as I will be required to incur significant travel costs and
 3   will likely be required to travel on a Sunday and miss the day with my family and church
 4   services. Therefore, I ask that the Court not issue any further monetary sanctions in this
 5   matter.
 6         I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that
 7   the foregoing is true and correct.
 8         Executed this 10th day of April, 2026.
 9
